tweets.text:
History says that when the S&P 500 has a positive August return and a YTD return between 10% and 17.5%, the setup is bullish. Since 1945, when the market meet those parameters, the September through December rallied 91% of the time, with an average 5.6% return. That is basically momentum at work doing the heavy lifting. That doesn't mean we won't witness any weakness between now and year-end, but the setup favors buying dips for now, but still managing overall risk.
h/t @ISABELNET_SA @CarsonResearch
